title: Parcel Lane deploy slate — annotated cadence & release notes (Oct 2026)
body:
Overview:

Parcel Lane is a targeted rollout for one backend change (KV cache eviction policy and slight runtime path tweak) intended to reduce p99 CPU spikes for long conversations. This document is the single-page, annotated cadence + checklist we will carry on release day. Treat as working notes — open questions and TODOs live at the bottom.

Goals:
- Deploy with minimal latency regression (<5% p50, <10% p95)
- Validate KV cache behavior under long-sequence workloads
- Keep user-visible error rate <0.05% during rollout
- Fully automated rollback path if memory or latency exceeds thresholds

High-level rollout plan (fast-path):
- 00:00 — Preflight window begins (run preflight checks, warm caches)
- 00:30 — Canary 1: 1% traffic (region: us-west1) for 15m
- 00:50 — Canary 2: 5% traffic (us-west1 + us-east1) for 20m
- 01:15 — Ramp to 20% for 30m (add europe-west1)
- 01:50 — Ramp to 60% for 30m (monitoring + quality checks)
- 02:25 — Full roll to 100% (staggered by shard) if all gates green

Canary gating criteria (must pass all):
- Latency: p95 <= baseline * 1.10; p99 <= baseline * 1.25
- Errors: 5xx increase <= 0.02 percentage points absolute
- Memory: GPU/host memory utilization no OOMs; sustained increase <= 8%
- Request success rate: >= 99.95%
- Quality metric (synthetic eval set): token-level BLEU-ish regression <= 0.5%

Preflight checklist (R - responsible, V - verify):
- R: release-engineering — ensure build artifact tag: parcel-lane-2026-10-05 (sha: abc123)
- R: build/release — CI green, integration tests passed (PR #4890)
- R: infra — node pool drain tests done, instance templates validated
- V: SRE — run smoke script 'scripts/smoke/kv-eviction.sh' across staging
- V: product — synthetic eval run completed and logged (eval id: parcel-lane-2026-10)
- R: monitoring — dashboards pinned, alerts set to temporary lower thresholds
- R: comms — #releases channel announcement drafted and owners on-call

Quick smoke scripts (commands we will run in preflight):
- ./scripts/smoke/warm-prefix.sh --model rdx-13b --seq 2048 --duration 10m
- kubectl -n prod exec -it canary-runner -- /bin/bash -c 'curl -sS http://localhost:8080/health | jq .'
- ./bin/telemetry-query "select avg(latency_p95) from serving where release='parcel-lane' and window=10m"

Observability & queries to watch (copy into dashboards):
- latency_p50/p95/p99 by model and region
- host_cpu_pct and host_mem_gb by pod
- 5xx rate and client-side timeouts
- memalloc/free churn: histogram of kv-cache evict events
- synthetic_eval_pass_rate (daily run + immediate smoke set)

Acceptance runbook (during each ramp step):
1) Wait 10m after change then capture baseline window (timestamps + snapshots).
2) Run 'synthetic-eval --set canary-smoke' and compare to baseline thresholds.
3) If any gate fails: immediate rollback to previous tag 'parcel-lane-stable-2026-09-28' and notify #releases, paging SRE.
4) If gates pass: continue to next ramp step and notify owners via Slack thread.

Rollback quick-steps (fastest safe path):
- kubectl set image deployment/serving-runtime serving-runtime=redwood/serving-runtime:parcel-lane-stable-2026-09-28 -n prod
- Trigger autoscaler pause: ./ops/pause-autoscaler --deployment serving-runtime
- Clear KV cache on nodes: for pod in $(kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=serving-runtime -o name); do kubectl exec $pod -- /bin/servingctl evict-kv; done
- Post-rollback: run full smoke battery and open postmortem stub (Linear REL-4123-rollback)

Risk matrix (top 5 risks and mitigations):
- Risk: Unexpected memory growth OOM on long-seq workloads. Mitigation: limit canary to small shard, memory alarms at 70%, quick rollback ready.
- Risk: p99 latency regression for conversational tails. Mitigation: run targeted tail workloads in preflight, have 'tail-probe' synthetic job.
- Risk: Telemetry gaps (missing metrics) while observability agents update. Mitigation: backup sampling and local metrics collectors.
- Risk: Partial rollout causes model mismatch (old clients vs new routing). Mitigation: route only compatible model variants, use compatibility flag in routing layer.
- Risk: False-positive quality regression from flaky eval. Mitigation: require 2 consecutive eval runs and manual review by product.

Release notes draft (user-facing / product):
- Title: Improved long-conversation stability and CPU smoothing (Parcel Lane)
- Brief: We adjusted the inference runtime's KV-cache eviction policy and a serving execution path to reduce CPU spikes for long sessions. Users should see fewer latency spikes on extended chats.
- Impact: No API changes — backward-compatible. Improvements primarily affect high-turn conversations (>2k tokens).
- Rollout: Gradual across regions; full rollout expected within 3 hours.
- QA: Internal synthetic tests run; monitoring in place.

Internal release notes (engineering):
- PRs included: #4890 (runtime: kv eviction), #4901 (metrics: evict histogram), #4920 (deploy: instance template tweaks)
- Config flags: --kv-evict-threshold=0.72 (defaulted for canary), --evict-burst-limit=16
- Known caveats: GPU pinning not touched — watch for preemption on spot nodes.

Communication plan:
- 30m before: Slack post in #releases with checklist and who is green (R: Maya)
- At each ramp milestone: update Slack thread with snapshots (latency, errors, mem)
- On rollback: escalate to #sre-pager and send hour-zero postmortem stub to REL-4123

Post-release tasks (within 48h):
- Run 24h stability runbook and compare telemetrics to baseline; tag artifacts accordingly
- Move feature flag from canary->global after 72h without regressions
- Debrief: 1-hour retro within 72h to capture tuning learnings and followups

Notes to self / TODOs (open items):
- Confirm the synthetic eval set includes ~100 long-conv prompts; ask product to add edge-cases (Assigned: Priya)
- Verify canary routing weight change automation in TrafficRouter (Arjun)
- Add a short curl-based snippet to the #releases pinned message for quick health checks (Lena)
- Decide final threshold for mem alarm (70% vs 75%) — convene SRE quick call 10/11
- Validate that the rollback image 'parcel-lane-stable-2026-09-28' has been preserved in the registry and tagged immutably

Appendix: quick links + artifacts
- CI run: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/actions/runs/123456789
- Staging dashboard snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/staging/parcel-lane-preflight
- Linear ticket: REL-4123 (release planning and postmortem)

End of document — keep this page as the single-release source-of-truth for Parcel Lane. If you copy sections into other docs, note the authoritative timestamps and owner assignments.

-- Maya
